## ggplot rules!

-- Think about your target audience

-- Think about your axes

-- Think about effective use of color

-- Think about the complete story you are trying to tell

-- Think about if the plot is appropriate for the data you have

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false 
library(tidyverse)
library(palmerpenguins)
```

## Warm-up

What is the difference between the `|>` and the `+`?

## Pipe

The pipe operator ("and then") takes an object and puts it as the value
of the first argument to the next function:

```         
data |>
   glimpse()

glimpse(data)
```

## +

The `+` is when we want to "add" onto our canvas! Our canvas is
`ggplot()`.

## Warm-up{.smaller}

What's gong on here?

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

```

## aes

variables -- maps \> `ggplot()`

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
ggplot(
  penguins,
  aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = bill_depth_mm)
) +
  geom_point(colour = "blue")
```

## aes

```{r}
#| echo: false
ggplot(
  penguins,
  aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = bill_depth_mm)
) +
  geom_point(colour = "blue")
```


Any time we want to change "non-data" aspects on the graph, it goes
outside the `aes()`

## aes positioning

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
ggplot(
  penguins,
  aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = bill_depth_mm)
) +
  geom_point(colour = "blue")
```

is the same as

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
ggplot(penguins) +
  geom_point(aes(x = bill_length_mm, 
                 y = bill_depth_mm),
                 colour = "blue")
```

## aes positioning

We ask ourselves whether we want an aesthetic mapping to apply to the
entire plot or only to a specific geometric layer.

## color

A common form of color blindness is red-green color blindness....

We can do a lot with color!

-- `scale_color_manual()`

-- `scale_color_gradient()`

-- `scale_color_viridis_()`

## colors

We can be very direct on where we want the color to go!

```         
scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Adelie" = "lightskyblue1",
      "Chinstrap" = "chartreuse3",
      "Gentoo" = "gold2"
    )
  )
```

## Extension Questions{.smaller}

The Portland Trailblazers are a National Basketball Association (NBA)
sports team. These data reflect the points scored by 9 Portland
Trailblazers players across the first 10 games of the 2021-2022 NBA
season.

Download the `trailblazer.csv` roster. Add this to your data folder in
the data-viz project, and upload these data into R. Our goal is to
re-create the following image (see next slide)

## 

```{r}
#| echo: false 
trailblazer <- read_csv("data/trailblazer21.csv")

new.blazer <- trailblazer |>  # save object as new.blazer
  pivot_longer( #make data longer
    cols = -Player, #bring all cols but Player down
    names_to = "Game", #name the col Game
    values_to = "Points", #name the values col Points
  ) |> 
  separate_wider_delim(Game , delim = "_", names = c("Game" , "Location"))

ggplot(
  new.blazer,
  aes(x = Game, y = Points, color = Location, group = 1)
) +
  geom_line(color = "gray70") +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~ Player) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Home" = "steelblue",
      "Away" = "darkorange"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Trail Blazers Player Performance Across Games",
    x = "Game",
    y = "Points Scored",
    color = "Location"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1))
```
